summary: Your caucus votes on you: Members of your own party in {the body} call a vote on whether you keep {your post}, after you broke with {party leader}.
realLife: One life: In February 2021 she kept her leadership post 145 to 61 in a secret ballot, and days later Wyoming's party censured her. In May she was removed by voice vote and replaced. Another: After he backed the Republican nominee in 2008, Senate Democrats voted 42 to 13 to let him keep his chairmanship, after President-elect Obama urged them not to punish him. He lost one committee seat. Another: When he joined the Democrats in 2009, they refused to let him keep his seniority on committees.
gates: You hold a party post or a chair in {the body}.
You broke with {party leader} on a recorded vote, endorsement or statement.
weights: How many members agree with you.

choices: make your case in a speech

branches.then: You keep the post by a wide margin. Days later your party at home censures you anyway.
